hypotheses.reasoning: The fault originates at the external identity provider (idp.example/oauth2/token) called by auth-svc. Starting around 05:39:12 (#182) its latency climbs from 4.5s to 11-13s (#183, #185), past the 2s soft threshold, and by 05:40:43 calls hang until the 30s timeout (#190, #204, #209). account-svc's AuthClient.issueToken calls to auth-svc POST /tokens then time out (#191, #205). Those hung calls hold account-svc's 50-connection pool to auth-svc, which saturates (queued requests and pool checkout timeouts), and edge-proxy returns 503s on POST /login. The pool saturation and the 503s are downstream symptoms and are not cited. accounts-db, session-cache and audit-consumer show no errors, so they are not the cause. A rate-limited client (#181) is minor noise. No 5xx or connection-refused responses come from the IdP, so this reads as a hang rather than an outage.

The identity provider could be treated as a third-party outage, since its failures persist for several minutes. The logs show slow then hung calls rather than fast 5xx or connection-refused errors, which favours dependency_timeout, so this is a lower-probability reading of the same lines.

verdict.recommendedAction: Escalate to the identity provider owners and check its status and latency. Meanwhile, shorten the auth-svc to IdP timeout (30s is too long) and add a circuit breaker so auth-svc fails fast. Also bound the account-svc to auth-svc connection pool and shed load at the edge, so a hung dependency does not exhaust the pool and cause 503s for all logins.
